text:
alex: Heads up — after last night's runtime deploy I'm seeing a mid-sized dip in prefix cache hit rate for a few long-prompt models. ~6-8% absolute on user-facing p95 paths. Repro'd in staging. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/prefix-cache

maya: saw this too. Quick profiler pass shows kernel selector is choosing the new attn micro-kernel for short-ish sequences which seems to change the canonicalization order for padded prefixes. Hit keys look different.

rohan: interesting — did the batching heuristics change? I noticed the scheduler now groups by seq_len_bin which can increase eviction pressure on the prefix cache if a burst of short requests bumps others out.

emily: did a flamegraph on staging. There's an extra memcpy in the KV path when the micro-kernel is used (something about packing ordering). That shifts timing and apparently the prefix-key normalization runs earlier, before whitespace normalization step we relied on.

alex: can we get a minimal repro? sample payloads I used: `model: phoenix-7b, seq_len: 48..200, priming: long role-play prompts`

maya: repro attached (small dump pasted):
```
CACHE_KEY: func(prefix, tokenizer_norm)
old_key: 0x8a7f3c
new_key: 0xe1b402  # differs when micro-kernel path taken
seq_len_bucket: 32
kernel_selected: micro_v2
```

rohan: timeline — runtime roll at 03:12 UTC introduced kernel-selector change (PR #4521). It flips a boolean to prefer microkernel for mem-opt paths. I think this is the strong suspect.

deploy-bot: deploy: runtime-service v2.14.0 rolled to prod (us-west1/us-east1) at 2025-11-12T03:12:07Z, triggered by: ci/cd/pipeline-789.

emily: confirmed via bisect: toggling `choose_microkernel=true` reintroduces the key mismatch. When false, prefix keys line up with baseline and hit-rate recovers.

alex: thanks. We should decide mitigation: rollback kernel selector, or add key-invariance shim. Thoughts?

rohan: quick mitigation — pin kernel selection for affected models (model whitelist) and enable a fallback salting policy for keys so different kernel orderings map to the same canonical key until we fix normalization. I prepared a patch to runtime config: 
```
prefix_cache:
  key_mode: canonical_v1
  kernel_pin:
    - phoenix-7b
    - atlas-3b
  salt_fallback: enabled
```

maya: that sounds good. Also want to add an e2e test that runs short/long seqs and asserts cache key invariants between kernel variants. Caught this too late because unit tests only exercised single kernel.

emily: root cause summary: micro-kernel changes internal packing order -> KV write order subtlely different -> our prefix-key function depended on iteration order (non-deterministic across kernels). Fix options: 1) make key func order-independent, 2) harmonize micro-kernel packing to previous ordering, or 3) pin kernels until we validate.

alex: plan: 1) roll a canary rollback for us-west at 04:00 UTC (I will schedule), 2) apply rohan's config patch for kernel pin + salt_fallback in prod for affected models, 3) add invariant e2e and unit tests, 4) follow-up RFC for kernel selector changes requiring key-invariance guarantee.

rohan: I'll open the patch PR and leave a rollback instruction in the release notes. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4698

maya: I'll write the e2e test and add to the CI matrix. Also adding a perf check to detect >2% hit-rate delta on canaries.

alex: awesome. @emily can you sketch the key-invariant algorithm? even a short note will help the RFC.

emily: sketch: compute two canonical hashes: one for token sequence order, one for ordered-by-token-value (sorted); combine with xor to get order-independent fingerprint. Pseudocode:
```
def canonical_key(tokens):
  h1 = hash(serialize(tokens))
  h2 = hash(serialize(sorted(tokens)))
  return h1 ^ h2
```
This is cheap and mitigates kernel-induced iteration differences. We'll validate collision rates with sampling.

alex: perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll post updates once the canary/patch are live. :thumbsup:
